primary_purpose: Absolute lower-body strength; force production that transfers to sprint/cut speed
cue: Brace the core by breathing into the belly. Drive the knees out as you lower down. Exhale on the way back up.

primary_purpose: Squat pattern competency for novices; equipment-limited substitute
cue: Same bracing/knee-out cue as back squat, at a lighter, more controllable load.

primary_purpose: Movement competency, warm-up, no-equipment option
cue: Brace the core. Drive the knees out.

primary_purpose: Posterior chain strength; hamstring/glute force for sprinting and cutting
cue: Brace the core. Drive the hips back. Stretch the glutes and hamstrings. Stay balanced on the feet.

primary_purpose: Hinge competency, hamstring loading, equipment-limited substitute
cue: Same hinge cue as trap bar deadlift, controlled tempo.

primary_purpose: Single-leg strength; addresses deep lunge mobility demand
cue: Step out and land soft — front knee tracks over the toes, back knee drops straight down like you're kneeling on a pillow. Push the front foot into the ground to stand back up.

primary_purpose: Frontal-plane strength for cutting and marking positions
cue: Sit back into the moving leg, knee over the ankle, and keep the trail leg long and straight. Push off the ground to reset back to center — don't just fall back.

primary_purpose: Throwing-adjacent upper-body power; leg-drive-assisted overhead power
cue: Dip, drive, and punch through the bar — legs start it, arms finish it. Full lockout overhead, ribs stay stacked over your hips, not flared out.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pressing strength; general upper-body power transfer
cue: Set your shoulder blades back and down before you unrack. Bar touches the chest under control, then drive it straight up — push the bar, not just your arms.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pressing strength; equipment-limited substitute, unilateral stability option
cue: Elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared out to the sides. Lower under control, press up and slightly in until the dumbbells nearly touch overhead.

primary_purpose: Vertical pressing strength; shoulder stability for throwing
cue: Brace the core hard before you press — this isn't just a shoulder exercise, it's a full-body one. Press straight up, and get your head through at the top.

primary_purpose: Vertical pressing strength; equipment-limited, unilateral option
cue: Brace like you're about to get hit, then press straight overhead — don't let your lower back arch to get the weight up.

primary_purpose: Upper-chest/shoulder pressing strength, throwing-adjacent
cue: Same press, different angle — this one hits the upper chest, so keep the bench angle moderate and press up and slightly back, not straight up.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight pressing competency; no-equipment option
cue: Straight line from head to heels — squeeze the glutes so the hips don't sag. Chest to the floor, then push the ground away hard.
notes: Regression is an Incline/Elevated Push-Up (not yet a library row — see gap list).

primary_purpose: Shoulder-friendly pressing angle; unilateral option
cue: Brace, then press the bar up and slightly forward along its natural arc. Keep the ribs down — don't let this turn into a back-extension exercise.

primary_purpose: Triceps/chest pressing strength
cue: Lean forward slightly, elbows tucked, lower under control until you feel a stretch in the shoulders — then press back up without flaring the elbows out.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pulling strength; shoulder health/balance for throwing volume
cue: Hinge at the hips, flat back, and pull the bar to your lower ribs — lead with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pulling strength; equipment-limited, unilateral option
cue: Brace through the core so your torso doesn't rotate with the pull. Row the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to the body, squeeze at the top.

primary_purpose: Vertical pulling strength; upper-body pulling capacity for contested catches/marking
cue: Start from a dead hang, shoulders engaged before you pull. Drive the elbows down and back, chin over the bar, and control the way down — don't just drop.

primary_purpose: Vertical pulling strength; equipment-limited substitute for pull-up
cue: Pull your shoulder blades down and back first, then bring the bar to your upper chest — think elbows to your back pockets, not just hands to the bar.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight horizontal pulling; no/low-equipment option
cue: Body in a straight line, chest to the bar, elbows pulling back and down. The more horizontal your body, the harder it gets — own your angle.

primary_purpose: Scapular health/posture; shoulder-health accessory for throwing volume
cue: Pull the band apart at chest height, squeezing the shoulder blades together like you're pinching a pencil between them. Slow and controlled — this one's about quality, not weight.

primary_purpose: Rear delt/rotator cuff health; shoulder health for throwing volume
cue: Pull to your face, not your chest — elbows high, hands finishing outside your ears like you're flexing. This is where we build shoulder health, not ego.

primary_purpose: Full-body explosive power (triple extension); converts strength into speed/jump ability
cue: Pull the slack out of the bar first — patient off the floor, then explode as it passes the knee. Extend tall through the hips, then get under it fast.

primary_purpose: Simplified pulling position; lower technical demand than full clean
cue: Set from the hang position, hips back, bar against the thighs. Snap the hips forward hard and violently, then get under the bar — this is the whole point of the lift, so attack it.

primary_purpose: Equipment-limited, lower-technical-demand entry point to the clean pattern
cue: Same hip snap as the barbell version, just with dumbbells in your hands — explode the hips, shrug hard, and catch it soft in the front rack.

primary_purpose: Full-body explosive power with overhead stability demand
cue: Same aggressive hip extension as the clean, but this time you're punching the bar straight overhead and dropping under it — commit to the catch, don't second-guess it.

primary_purpose: Simplified snatch entry point
cue: From the hang, snap the hips through violently and pull yourself under the bar fast — overhead lockout should feel active, not passive.

primary_purpose: Builds pulling power without the catch-phase technical demand
cue: This is all about the finish — pull the bar close, extend tall through the hips, shoulders shrugging at the very top. No catch, just pure extension.

primary_purpose: Explosive overhead power via leg drive
cue: Dip straight down, drive straight up, and punch the bar to lockout as you drop under it slightly. Legs do the work — don't try to press it with your arms.

primary_purpose: Hip-hinge-based explosive power; lowest-technical-demand entry to ballistic hip extension
cue: Hinge and hike the bell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward hard to float the weight up — the arms are just along for the ride.
notes: RETIRED: duplicate of HG-007 Kettlebell Swing (Russian).

primary_purpose: Rotational core control for throwing
cue: Brace like someone's about to poke you in the stomach, then press the band straight out and resist it pulling your torso around. If your hips rotate, you've lost the rep.

primary_purpose: Converts rotational strength into throwing-specific power
cue: Load into your back hip, then whip the ball across your body into the wall — this should feel explosive, like you're throwing a punch with your whole torso.

primary_purpose: Foundational trunk stability for layout and throwing mechanics
cue: Squeeze the glutes, brace the abs, and keep a dead straight line from shoulders to heels. If your hips sag or pike up, reset.

primary_purpose: Novice-friendly anti-extension core control
cue: Brace the core flat into the floor — no arch in the low back. Lower the opposite arm and leg slow and controlled, then bring them back without losing the brace.

primary_purpose: Advanced anti-extension core strength
cue: Brace hard before you roll out — only go as far as you can keep your low back from arching. Pull back in with the abs, not the arms.

primary_purpose: Hip/oblique control relevant to cutting and marking
cue: Stack your shoulders and hips, and lift through the waist — don't let the hips sag toward the floor. Hold it like you mean it.

primary_purpose: Anti-lateral flexion under asymmetric load
cue: Stand tall, brace hard, and don't let the weight pull you over to one side — walk with control, not a lean.

primary_purpose: Total-body loaded carry; grip and trunk stability, general work capacity
cue: Chest up, shoulders back, brace the core like you're bracing for a hit — walk tall and don't let the weight round your shoulders forward.

primary_purpose: Advanced anti-extension/hip flexor core strength
cue: Hang tall, brace the ribs down, and curl the hips up toward you — this is a core exercise, not a hip flexor swinging contest, so control the tempo.

primary_purpose: Vertical power for layout, blocks, contested catches
cue: Load quick, swing the arms, and explode up onto the box — land soft with the knees bent, don't just jump up and let it slam.

primary_purpose: Reactive strength / stretch-shortening-cycle development — minimizing ground-contact time on landing
cue: Step off, don't jump off — land, and the instant your feet touch, explode back up as fast as you can. Ground contact should be quick, not a pause.

primary_purpose: Frontal-plane power for cutting and marking
cue: Load and push off one leg, land soft and stuck on the other — stick the landing before you bound back the other way.

primary_purpose: Unilateral reactive strength; transfers to single-leg takeoffs for layout/blocks
cue: Load on one leg, drive up or out explosively, and land under control — balance the landing before you reset for the next rep.

primary_purpose: Reactive strength; rhythm and ground-contact time development
cue: Quick ground contacts — think 'hot coals,' minimal time on the floor between hurdles. Stay tall, don't collapse at the knees.

primary_purpose: Horizontal power for layout distance and acceleration
cue: Load the hips back, swing the arms hard, and jump for maximum distance — land soft with the knees bent and stick it.

primary_purpose: Upper-body explosive power; full-body deceleration/reset pattern
cue: Reach the ball high overhead, then whip it down into the ground as hard as you can, using your whole body, not just your arms.

primary_purpose: Upper-body explosive pressing power
cue: Load into the chest, then punch the ball straight out explosively — this should feel like you're pushing someone off of you.

primary_purpose: Tendon-pain regression entry point
cue: Hold position, brace, steady breathing.

primary_purpose: Deep-cut sprinting demand
cue: Stay low, drive the knees forward and down hard, and keep your shin angle consistent — this is about building the pattern before we ever add speed.

primary_purpose: Full-speed sprinting demand
cue: Tall posture, quick ground contacts, and relaxed shoulders — sprinting fast is as much about staying loose as it is about pushing hard.

primary_purpose: Knee drive and ground-contact patterning
cue: Drive the knee up to hip height, punch it down actively into the ground — quick and rhythmic, not a slow high-knee march.

primary_purpose: Hamstring/leg-cycling patterning
cue: Same knee drive as an A-skip, but now extend the leg out in front before punching it down — stay tall and rhythmic.

primary_purpose: Acceleration mechanics; teaches forward lean and shin angle at the start
cue: Start tall, fall forward until you have to catch yourself, then drive out low and hard — let gravity start you, then attack.

primary_purpose: Acceleration-specific overload; force production in the drive phase
cue: Stay low, drive hard through the ground, and keep the shin angle aggressive the whole way — the sled should never pull you upright early.

primary_purpose: Top-end/max-velocity mechanics
cue: Build into your top speed gradually before the marked zone, then relax and let your legs turn over fast — trying to force speed usually slows you down.

primary_purpose: Acceleration mechanics from a game-realistic starting position (deep-cut starts)
cue: Explosive first step, low shin angle, and drive — don't pop straight up out of the start, stay low and build.

primary_purpose: Landing/deceleration mechanics for layout and cutting
cue: Land soft with bent knees and hips back, like you're sitting into a chair — absorb the landing before you do anything else with it.
